paragraph: Waldwick's single-family market is a real seller's market. Thirty-eight sales over six months at a median of $722,500, a sale-to-list ratio of 1.09, roughly 89 percent of homes closing above list, and a median of 12 days on market. That combination means multiple offer situations are common, and the typical sale is a four-bedroom colonial or cape with two full baths. Monthly counts are small enough that individual months are noise, but the direction is clear: medians moved from $615,000 in February up to the mid $770,000s in June and July, so the town is tracking the normal spring-into-summer climb without any sign of the usual late-summer softening yet. Condos and townhouses are a much thinner slice with 7 sales at a median of $550,000, mostly two-bedroom, two-bath townhouses, and they are competitive too at a 1.04 ratio and 18 days on market. Multi-family activity is three two-family sales at a median of $1.1 million, too few to draw conclusions from. If you're comparing tiers, the deciding factor isn't market heat, because both moving tiers are tight. It's whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family, the low-maintenance lifestyle of a townhouse, or the rental income of a two-family.
